title: Evidence Tier Claim Checker
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Judge the evidence behind ten fictional vendor claims by placing each in one of five evidence levels, from Strong to No evidence of effect.

learningObjectives: The learner will judge the strength of the evidence behind ten vendor claims by assigning each to one of five evidence levels, correctly placing at least eight of ten on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Evidence-based practice, randomized controlled trial, selection bias, and the five evidence levels, from Chapter 2.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge, commit an answer, and read the reason
keyQuestions: Does a large sample make a claim strong?
commonMisconceptions: A large sample makes a claim strong whatever the study design
Teacher satisfaction is evidence of learning
Any before-and-after gain shows the program worked
assessmentOpportunities: Which level is a teacher satisfaction survey?
Does a large self-selected sample make a claim Strong?

controls.name: Five level buttons
controls.description: Choose Strong, Moderate, Promising, Demonstrates a rationale, or No evidence of effect for the current claim.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: Shows or hides the one-line definition of each level.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: Moves to the next claim after feedback.

controls.name: Previous missed and Next missed
controls.description: On the results screen, step through the claims you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: Reshuffles the claims for a practice run.
